title: WWII PUBLICATIONS ETC
findings: Title is only 'WWII PUBLICATIONS ETC'. Photo 1 shows six wartime Australian Army-looking items: four cardboard postal boxes printed 'KHAKI and GREEN..', 'STAND EASY', 'ACTIVE SERVICE' and 'JUNGLE WARFARE' (each has a printed box panel at top right that looks like a postage-paid stamp box and a stuck-on typed or handwritten dispatch label, text not legible at this resolution); a red cloth hardback 'SOLDIERING ON' with a crest and small print at the lower right that I could not read; and a torn paper-covered booklet titled 'VICTORY' (script above it appears to read 'New Guinea') with an orange sunburst badge (looks like the Army Rising Sun) at the lower edge. No publisher, date or edition is legible, so WWII dating is plausible from style and badge but not confirmed. Photos 2 and 3 are close-ups of a glossy concert poster that the title does not mention at all: 'Live in Concert - DON McLEAN - America's Music Legend - featuring American Pie, Vincent, Crying and much more... - A John L Hansen - Event Entertainment Presentation', with a black pen signature reading 'Don McLean' on the white strip at the foot. The signature looks like a continuous ink line with varied pressure rather than a printed dot pattern, but this is a low-resolution photo and there is no certificate, dedication, date or witness, so it is unverified. I could not research the boxed series or signed-poster values (web search budget was used up), so the strength rests on the photos only.
condition: Poster is glossy with visible fold lines and ripples, no tears seen. Boxes are worn, stained and creased, with a torn corner on ACTIVE SERVICE and a chipped corner on JUNGLE WARFARE; contents of the boxes are not shown. VICTORY booklet is torn, stained and missing a piece at the lower edge. SOLDIERING ON cover looks sound with some rubbing.
reason: Under-described 'etc': a Don McLean concert poster with an apparent hand signature (unverified, no COA) plus five WWII Australian service publications in original postal boxes.
marks_read: Signature 'Don McLean' (black pen, on poster foot); poster credit 'A John L Hansen - Event Entertainment Presentation'; box titles Khaki and Green, Stand Easy, Active Service, Jungle Warfare; book 'Soldiering On'; booklet 'Victory'. No dates or hallmarks.

title: QUANTITY OF ART POTTERY PLATES...

findings: About 20 pieces of handmade glazed studio-style pottery. Photo 1 overview: a large dark charger with blue, brown and gold streaky glaze at the back; about 9 to 10 black plates and saucers with red and blue splash glaze in two sizes; at least 2 (possibly 4) cream plates with painted pink flowers and a black half glaze; 2 matching mugs in the same floral and navy glaze; a small grey cup with a gold rim that looks like a different, commercial piece; 2 stacked bowls (blue and cream floral interior with a purple-brown rim, lower bowl with a green and cream swirl exterior); and a large yellow-rimmed pierced footed bowl or colander with a blue interior and two applied rolled handles. The catalogue names Jill Spencer and Catherine Batten, but the photos do not show which pieces are theirs, so the attributions are unverified, and I could not research the potters (web search budget was used up). condition: No chips or cracks visible on the faces shown. Glaze pitting and bubbles on the black plates (look like part of the glaze effect). Handle ends on the pierced bowl show raw clay (looks like the design but worth checking for breaks). Undersides and rims not fully checked.
reason: Large lot of handmade studio pottery with two named potters in the title; attribution unverified (no marks visible) but the quality is good and it could be worth more than a general lot price if the names are collectable.

title: ORIGINAL FRUIT BOX LABELS
findings: Photos show about three spiral-bound albums or folders holding labels in plastic sleeves, plus at least eight loose stacks of crisp labels that look unused. Legible labels: LALLA Brand Fancy Apples in gold foil and white versions ('Produce of Tasmania Australia', 'Grown and packed by W.A.G. Walker & Sons, Riverside, Tamar Valley, Tasmania', blue 'Quality' seal); 'Fancy Pears' labels in blue and green; magenta and white labels reading 'TAS FRU...' (partly legible) with a stylised F and leaf; a 'Southern Isle Pre-cooled Tasmania' card or album cover; DOLLAR BIRD APPLES 'Selected for Export' (The Producers Co-operative Distributing Society Ltd, Sydney NSW, and at Leeton, Kentucky, Adelaide, Brisbane, Devonport (Tas), Melbourne); BLUE BIRD Canadian Products (Distributors Sales Service Limited, Kelowna BC, packed and shipped by Crown Fruit Co. Ltd, Kelowna, with an Empire star); TWIN W Brand (Wells & Wade Fruit Company, Wenatchee, Washington, contents 40 lbs net); and BUY ME Brand Canadian Apples ('Volume bushel', tiny foot imprint that looks like 'Litho'd in Canada'). The bright lithography and crisp edges suggest genuine printed stock rather than modern reprints, though this is not certain from photos. No dates legible. The quantity cannot be counted but is likely well over 100 labels. Fruit crate labels from Tasmania, NSW, Canada and Washington State are a recognised collecting niche. I could not check market prices (web search budget was used up).
condition: Labels look bright and clean with sharp corners and the loose stacks look unused. Plastic sleeves have glare and a few creases; album covers are plain card or plastic with spiral binding. Backs of labels not shown.
reason: Large collection of original fruit crate labels (Tasmanian, NSW, Canadian and Washington State), many apparently unused stock, in albums; a collectors' niche and the quantity is unknown.
marks_read: Printed label text only: W.A.G. Walker & Sons (Riverside, Tamar Valley, Tasmania); Producers Co-operative Distributing Society Ltd (Sydney); Crown Fruit Co. Ltd / Distributors Sales Service Ltd (Kelowna BC); Wells & Wade Fruit Co (Wenatchee WA). No dates.
